newsitem.title: USA: SangStat says follow-up tests are positive.
newsitem.headline: SangStat says follow-up tests are positive.

text.p: SangStat Medical Corp Monday said one-year follow-up examinations of patient tests of Thymoglobulin, a drug used in kidney transplants, showed a graft survival rate of 83.5 percent.
In a statement, SangStat compared results to Pharmacia & Upjohn Inc's ATGAM, which has a 75.2 percent success rate when used to reverse acute kidney transplant rejection.

The follow-up tests tracked patients from Phase III tests of Thymoglobulin. The U.S. Food and Drug Administration currently is reviewing Thymoglobulin for approval. The FDA has not yet seen data from the follow-up tests, SangStat said.
SangStat shares were up 1 at 26-5/8 by mid-morning.

One year post-rejection treatment follow-up of the patients who received Thymoglobulin included assessments of graft survival, patient survival, incidence of malignancy, and incidence of recurrent rejection.

Results suggest that treatment with Thymoglobulin was associated with a significantly higher rejection reversal rate, a significantly greater prolongation in T cell depletion and significantly less recurrent rejection in the 90 days following anti-rejection therapy.
